Why Hollywood Can't Stop Casting Robert Pattinson

10Parts

Hook

Top hooks, yt-script score

  • 9In 2019 fans signed a petition to get him fired as Batman. In 2026 he became James Bond.
  • 8The sparkly vampire from Twilight is now 007. Here's how that actually happened.
  • 7He mocked his own billion-dollar franchise, then spent fifteen years making films nobody watched. It worked.

Look and device

Running device

A running 'DOUBTERS vs BELIEVERS' scoreboard in the top-left corner that flips as the story moves, plus a tuxedo bow tie that appears in every act (on a hanger, a poster, a shop window) until he finally wears it.

Look

Showbiz rise story in the house 2D style, Gumball/t-shirt character style (big white eyes, nose, ears), painterly detailed plates: a London street in Barnes, a castle film set, a screaming premiere, an arthouse cinema, a New York night street, a lighthouse, a Gotham rooftop in rain, a box-office board, a podcast studio, a London screen-test stage, an Amazon-style boardroom, a premiere red carpet. Real people stylised, no likeness, no real logos or film posters (generic shapes, titles as text only). Reported details tagged REPORTED unless confirmed. SFX under VO, music at combine.

Cold open

0:41 · 5 shots · 98 words
  1. 0.01WIDE8.7s

    May 2019. Warner Bros. names its new Batman, and within hours thousands of fans sign a petition to get him fired.

    Night Gotham-style skyline; a bat signal flickers on; phones light up below with angry thumbs-down.

    MAY 2019

    ANIMATIONBat signal flickers; petition counter ticks up fast.

  2. 0.02MED8.3s

    The complaint was simple. This was the sparkly vampire from Twilight. The boy who girls screamed at. Not a superhero.

    Angry fans hold signs NOT OUR BATMAN; a cardboard cut-out of a glittering vampire gets waved about.

    "NOT OUR BATMAN"

    ANIMATIONSigns bob; glitter sparkles on the cut-out.

  3. 0.03MED8.7s

    Seven years later, on the sixteenth of November 2026, Amazon made an announcement. Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond.

    Smash cut: a press screen flips to a silhouette in a tuxedo; 007 slams in; flashbulbs.

    16 NOV 2026 · 007

    ANIMATIONScreen flips; 007 slams; scoreboard flips to BELIEVERS.

  4. 0.04MED9.4s

    Same man. Same face. So what changed? Because Hollywood didn't hand him this. He spent fifteen years making sure they couldn't say no.

    Split frame: the vampire on the left, the tuxedo on the right; a question mark swings between them.

    SAME MAN?

    ANIMATIONQuestion mark swings like a pendulum.

  5. 0.05TITLE5.7s

    This is how a Twilight punchline became the most wanted actor in Hollywood.

    Title over a bow tie spinning down onto a vampire cape.

    WHY HOLLYWOOD CAN'T STOP CASTING ROBERT PATTINSON

    ANIMATIONBow tie spins down, lands, glints.

Act 1: The London Kid

0:42 · 4 shots · 103 words
  1. 1.01WIDE12.4s

    Robert Pattinson was born in London in May 1986 and grew up in Barnes, by the Thames. His dad imported vintage cars from America. His mum worked at a modelling agency.

    A leafy Barnes street by the river; a shiny old American car rolls past a terrace; a boy watches from a gate.

    LONDON · 1986

    ANIMATIONCar rolls in with turning wheels; ducks on the river.

  2. 1.02MED10.6s

    He wasn't a stage-school kid. He joined a local amateur drama club as a teenager, by his own account partly because that's where the girls were.

    A small church-hall stage; a teenage boy in a too-big costume blinks in a spotlight; a scoreboard tag: REPORTED (HIS WORDS).

    BARNES THEATRE CLUB

    ANIMATIONSpotlight swings onto him; he shrugs.

  3. 1.03MED11.3s

    In 2005 that hobby turned into Harry Potter. He played Cedric Diggory, the golden Hogwarts champion in The Goblet of Fire, the one who doesn't make it out.

    A castle film set: a teen in a yellow-and-black champion's jersey holds a golden cup; a camera crane swoops.

    2005 · CEDRIC DIGGORY

    ANIMATIONCup glints; crane swoops; a sad trombone sting on 'doesn't make it out'.

  4. 1.04MED7.5s

    Remember the producer on that film, David Heyman. He'll come back at the very end of this story.

    A producer with a clipboard by the camera gives a thumbs up; a tiny bow tie sits on his clipboard. Name tag DAVID HEYMAN.

    DAVID HEYMAN · PRODUCER

    ANIMATIONName tag pops in; bow tie glints on the clipboard.

Act 2: The Twilight Trap

0:36 · 4 shots · 87 words
  1. 2.01WIDE6.8s

    Then in 2008 came the part that changed everything. Edward Cullen, the brooding vampire in Twilight.

    A misty pine forest; a pale figure in a jacket stands in a shaft of light, skin sparkling.

    2008 · TWILIGHT

    ANIMATIONMist drifts; skin sparkles on 'vampire'.

  2. 2.02MED8.7s

    Five films. More than three billion dollars at the box office. Screaming crowds at every premiere, and paparazzi outside his door.

    A premiere carpet; a wall of screaming fans with banners; flashbulbs pop; a counter rolls to $3,000,000,000+.

    5 FILMS · $3B+

    ANIMATIONCounter rolls; flashes pop in rhythm with screams.

  3. 2.03MED10.6s

    And here's the strange part. He never really pretended to love it. In interviews he joked about the films so often that it became his trademark.

    A chat-show sofa; he laughs and shrugs while a host looks horrified; little joke bubbles float up.

    "HE MOCKED HIS OWN HIT"

    ANIMATIONBubbles float up; host's jaw drops.

  4. 2.04MED9.8s

    Critics, meanwhile, had him down as a pretty face who'd fade away when the franchise ended. Hollywood has seen that story a hundred times.

    A row of critics in a screening room hold up low score cards: 2, 3, 2; a gravestone-shaped poster labelled 'TEEN IDOL'.

    "ONE-HIT HEARTTHROB"

    ANIMATIONScore cards flip up one by one; scoreboard flips to DOUBTERS.

Act 3: The Weird Years

0:47 · 4 shots · 118 words
  1. 3.01MED11.3s

    So when Twilight wrapped in 2012, he did the opposite of what a heartthrob is supposed to do. He went looking for the strangest directors he could find.

    He walks past a shiny blockbuster poster and turns down a dark alley towards an arthouse cinema with a flickering sign.

    2012 · THE U-TURN

    ANIMATIONWalk cycle; poster glows then he turns away.

  2. 3.02MED7.9s

    David Cronenberg, twice. James Gray. Claire Denis. Small films, odd films, films that most of his fans never saw.

    A notice board of tiny film cards pins itself up one by one, each with a director's name; a lone fan in the cinema eats popcorn, confused.

    CRONENBERG · GRAY · DENIS

    ANIMATIONCards pin in on each name; popcorn spills.

  3. 3.03MED14.3s

    The turning point was a film called Good Time in 2017. He played a desperate small-time crook running through New York for one terrible night, and critics finally said it out loud. This man can act.

    Neon New York night street; a bleached-hair crook sprints past bodegas; a critic's card flips from 2 to 9.

    2017 · GOOD TIME

    ANIMATIONRun cycle, neon flicker, card flips on 'act'.

  4. 3.04MED13.9s

    Then came The Lighthouse, where he and Willem Dafoe slowly lose their minds on a rock in the sea. Then Christopher Nolan cast him in Tenet, in a sharp suit, doing spy work. Sound familiar?

    A storm-lashed lighthouse; waves crash; then a whip pan to a sleek spy in a suit adjusting cufflinks, a bow tie peeking from his pocket.

    THE LIGHTHOUSE · TENET

    ANIMATIONWaves crash; whip pan; bow tie peeks out.

Act 4: Not Our Batman

0:40 · 4 shots · 99 words
  1. 4.01MED9.8s

    Which brings us back to 2019, and that petition. Matt Reeves wanted him for Batman. A big part of the internet wanted anyone else.

    A director in a cap holds out a bat cowl; a giant scroll of signatures unrolls behind him and keeps unrolling.

    MATT REEVES · 2019

    ANIMATIONScroll unrolls endlessly; paper SFX.

  2. 4.02WIDE9.4s

    The Batman came out in March 2022. Rain-soaked, slow, gloomy, and very good. It made about seven hundred and seventy million dollars worldwide.

    Gotham rooftop in pouring rain; a caped figure stands by a gargoyle; lightning; box-office counter rolls to ~$770M.

    THE BATMAN · ~$770M

    ANIMATIONRain streaks; cape flutters; lightning on 'very good'.

  3. 4.03MED10.2s

    The petition crowd went quiet. Some of them even started calling him Battinson. The doubters had been proven wrong in front of the whole world.

    The angry fans from the cold open slowly lower their NOT OUR BATMAN signs and flip them to BATTINSON.

    "BATTINSON"

    ANIMATIONSigns flip; scoreboard flips to BELIEVERS.

  4. 4.04MED10.9s

    A sequel, The Batman Part Two, has been delayed again and again, and is now due in February 2028. Remember that date, because it becomes a problem.

    A calendar on a wall flips pages: 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028; it lands on FEB 2028 with a red circle.

    PART II · FEB 2028

    ANIMATIONPages flip with whooshes; red circle draws itself.

Act 5: The Year Nobody Can Match

0:58 · 5 shots · 144 words
  1. 5.01MED13.2s

    Now look at his 2026. In April came The Drama, an A24 film with Zendaya. It opened on Easter weekend against Mario, and still crossed a hundred million dollars worldwide in nineteen days.

    A cinema foyer; a small indie poster stands next to a giant cartoon plumber poster; a counter races past $100M; 19 DAYS badge.

    THE DRAMA · $100M IN 19 DAYS

    ANIMATIONCounter races; plumber poster wobbles.

  2. 5.02MED12.4s

    A24 said more than eighty per cent of the audience came because of the two stars on the poster. That is the number that makes studio bosses pick up the phone.

    Pie chart fills to 80%+; an executive in a corner office lunges for a ringing phone.

    80%+ CAME FOR THE STARS

    ANIMATIONPie fills; phone rings; exec grabs it.

  3. 5.03WIDE11.7s

    Then in July, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. Pattinson played Antinous, the arrogant suitor trying to take Odysseus's house. It became Universal's biggest film of all time, passing Jurassic World.

    An ancient Greek hall with long tables and torches; a smug suitor lounges on a couch with a goblet; a dinosaur-shaped trophy gets knocked off a shelf by a ship-shaped one.

    THE ODYSSEY · UNIVERSAL'S #1

    ANIMATIONTorches flicker; trophy knocked off on 'passing'.

  4. 5.04MED10.9s

    In September he played the TV host Chris Hansen in Primetime. Critics loved it. The real Chris Hansen gave his performance a D on his own podcast.

    A news set with studio lights; a host character at a desk; then a podcast mic and a big red D grade card stamps down.

    PRIMETIME · GRADE: D

    ANIMATIOND card stamps with a thud.

  5. 5.05MED9.8s

    And on the eighteenth of December, he's a shape-shifting villain in Dune: Part Three, for director Denis Villeneuve. Keep that name in mind too.

    Desert dunes at dusk; a cloaked figure's face ripples and changes; name tag DENIS VILLENEUVE on a director's chair.

    DUNE: PART THREE · 18 DEC

    ANIMATIONFace ripples; sand blows across the frame.

Act 6: When It Goes Wrong

0:30 · 3 shots · 74 words
  1. 6.01MED9.4s

    To be fair, not everything works. Mickey 17, from the director of Parasite, cost about a hundred and eighteen million dollars to make.

    A sci-fi set with ice and clones; several identical men in parkas wave; a price tag $118M dangles.

    MICKEY 17 · $118M BUDGET

    ANIMATIONClones wave in sequence; price tag swings.

  2. 6.02MED9.4s

    It opened to just nineteen million in America, and Variety reported it was on course to lose around seventy-five million dollars in cinemas.

    A box-office board flickers; the number drops; a red arrow nosedives; source tag VARIETY.

    ~$75M LOSS (REPORTED)

    ANIMATIONArrow nosedives with a falling whistle.

  3. 6.03MED11.3s

    But here's the thing studios notice. When his films flop, the blame never seems to land on him. Critics usually say he was the best thing in it.

    A pile of mud thrown at a poster misses him and splats on the budget sign instead; a critic's card reads 'BEST THING IN IT'.

    "BEST THING IN IT"

    ANIMATIONMud splats on the sign, not him.

Act 7: Why Hollywood Keeps Calling

0:42 · 4 shots · 103 words
  1. 7.01MED11.7s

    So why does Hollywood keep calling? Reason one: the directors. Nolan twice, Villeneuve, Reeves, Bong Joon Ho, Robert Eggers, the Safdies. The best filmmakers keep picking the same man.

    A round table of director figures in caps and scarves all point at one empty chair with his name on it.

    REASON 1 · THE DIRECTORS

    ANIMATIONEach director's name tag pops on its word.

  2. 7.02MED11.3s

    Reason two: he works in both lanes. A small film he can turn into a hit. A giant blockbuster where he steals scenes. Most stars only manage one.

    A two-lane road: a little indie scooter in one lane, a huge blockbuster lorry in the other; he hops between them.

    REASON 2 · BOTH LANES

    ANIMATIONVehicles roll with turning wheels.

  3. 7.03MED10.6s

    Reason three: he's a producer now, finding young directors himself. And reason four: the internet loves him. Every chaotic interview and every meme is free advertising.

    His laptop pings with scripts; then a phone screen fills with laughing reaction faces and hearts.

    REASON 3 + 4

    ANIMATIONHearts float up; ping SFX.

  4. 7.04MED8.3s

    And the biggest reason is trust. You might not love a Robert Pattinson film. But it is almost never boring.

    A cinema audience leans forward together; nobody yawns; a big TRUST badge lands on the screen.

    NEVER BORING

    ANIMATIONAudience leans in; badge lands.

Act 8: The Name Is Pattinson

0:46 · 4 shots · 114 words
  1. 8.01WIDE12.8s

    Which brings us to Bond. In 2025 the Broccoli family handed creative control of 007 to Amazon MGM. Their pick for director? Denis Villeneuve. The writer? Steven Knight, who created Peaky Blinders.

    A grand old office; a set of golden keys with a 007 tag is handed across a desk to a sleek new executive; name tags pop.

    AMAZON MGM · VILLENEUVE · KNIGHT

    ANIMATIONKeys pass hand to hand; names pop.

  2. 8.02MED9.1s

    And one of the producers is David Heyman, the same man who watched a teenage Pattinson play Cedric Diggory twenty years earlier.

    The producer from act 1, now grey-haired, holds up the same clipboard with the tiny bow tie and smiles.

    DAVID HEYMAN · AGAIN

    ANIMATIONBow tie on the clipboard glints.

  3. 8.03MED12.1s

    The Hollywood Reporter said he screen-tested in London over the weekend of the twenty-fourth of October. Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult were all in the race.

    A London screen-test stage with a lone camera and light; five silhouettes wait on chairs; one steps into the light.

    SCREEN TEST · LONDON (REPORTED)

    ANIMATIONLight swings; silhouettes; one steps forward.

  4. 8.04MED12.1s

    Three weeks later, it was official. He called it the honour of a lifetime. The seventh actor to play James Bond, and the first ever chosen without the Broccoli family.

    He finally ties the bow tie that has followed him all video; a 007 logo-style card slides in; the scoreboard flips to BELIEVERS for good.

    THE 7TH JAMES BOND

    ANIMATIONBow tie tied; card slides; confetti.

Act 9: Batman or Bond?

0:50 · 4 shots · 126 words
  1. 9.01MED11.7s

    There is one big problem. Batman Part Two is still filming into 2027 and doesn't come out until February 2028. Bond is expected to start shooting in 2027 too.

    He stands between two doors: a dark bat door and a sleek 007 door; two calendars on the wall overlap in red.

    BATMAN AND BOND?

    ANIMATIONCalendars slide together; overlap glows red.

  2. 9.02MED8.3s

    Neither studio has said how they'll share him. One man, two of the biggest franchises on the planet, one diary.

    Two executives tug on the same diary from either side; he stands in the middle looking at his watch.

    ONE MAN · ONE DIARY

    ANIMATIONTug-of-war wobble; diary pages flutter.

  3. 9.03MED18.4s

    But think about where this started. Seven years ago, people signed petitions to keep him out of a cape. Now he's the face of Britain's most famous spy. He didn't get lucky. He spent fifteen years making strange choices with great directors, until nobody could say no.

    The petition scroll from act 4 rolls back up and turns into a 007 ticket; he walks into a golden spotlight.

    HE DIDN'T GET LUCKY

    ANIMATIONScroll rolls up; spotlight warms.

  4. 9.04CARD12.1s

    So, Batman or Bond? If he had to pick one, which should it be? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to Stormi Explain Everything for more stories like this.

    End card; last 5 s clean for end screen.

    BATMAN OR BOND?

    ANIMATIONEnd card slides up; then clean.

Fact log

Fixes against the transcript

  • Source predates the 16 Nov 2026 Amazon MGM announcement (Amazon, 007.com, ABC, NBC): Pattinson IS the new Bond; source's 'my gut says Callum Turner' prediction dropped.
  • Screen test weekend of 24 Oct 2026 = THR (unnamed sources), tagged REPORTED. 'Villeneuve personally asked him' (World of Reel) cut as unconfirmed.
  • The Batman Part II now 18 Feb 2028 (Variety), not 1 Oct 2027 as the source says.
  • The Odyssey passed Jurassic World ($1.677B) as Universal's biggest ever (Universal/NBCU, Sept 2026); source's '~1.8B' and '65% international' not stated as exact.
  • The Drama: ~$14M US opening, #3, $100M WW in 19 days, 5th A24 film over $100M, 80%+ came for the stars (Screen Daily / A24).
  • Mickey 17: $118M budget, $19.1M US opening, ~$75-80M projected theatrical loss (Variety, a source disputed it): tagged REPORTED.
  • Chris Hansen gave the performance a D on Have a Seat with Chris Hansen (AV Club, TMZ).
  • Die My Love numbers, Here Comes the Flood, 'two-lane star' budgets and A24 UK record not verified: cut.
  • 'Seventh actor' + 'first not chosen by the Broccolis' from launch coverage (ABC/IBTimes); Amazon took creative control 2025.
  • Twilight saga 'more than $3 billion' (5 films, widely reported ~$3.3B). Barnes upbringing, dad's vintage-car import business, drama club 'for the girls' are from his own interviews: framed as his account.
  • Real people stylised, no likeness, no real logos or posters.

Removed from the transcript

  • Rewritten from scratch in our own words (source ~3,600 words, ours ~1,600).
  • Updated for the official Bond casting (16 Nov 2026), which happened after the source was posted.
  • Prediction section, Gary Oldman/TMZ/Brosnan/Danny Boyle rumours cut.
  • Unverified numbers cut (see FACT_FIXES).
